newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Aircraft expects return to profitability.
newsitem.headline: Israel Aircraft expects return to profitability.

text.p: State-owned Israel Aircraft Industries (IAI) expects to return to profitability in 1997 after 10 years of losses, chairman Avigdor Ben-Gal said on Tuesday.
"We're predicting a profit of one to two percent of sales," he told Reuters.
He said IAI was forecasting revenues of $1.6 billion this year, compared with an estimated $1.48 billion in 1996. Exports are expected to reach $1.2 billion this year, up from $1.1 billion in 1996.

IAI officials would not say how big the 1996 loss would be but said the company, a maker of aviation and aerospace equipment, had lost money for the last 10 years. In recent years, however, IAI has not published financial statements.
IAI has been hit by a sharp drop in orders from the Israeli Defence Ministry in recent years as well as the worldwide downturn in defence budgets.

A reorganisation plan in the early 1990s led to the layoffs of thousands of workers and in Sepember parliament approved a debt reorganisation plan for IAI. Under it, banks rescheudled debts of $300 million and provided $120 million in new credit, while the government boosted its equity by $122 million.
